idee_recherchee.texte: Einstein's general relativity describes gravity as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy, where massive objects like stars and black holes bend the fabric around them and other objects follow those curved paths.

titre_video: Scientists Are Freaking Out Over Space Time (It's Not Real)
titre: Lentille gravitationnelle et ombre de l'horizon des événements
resume: Gravity warps space-time so light from the accretion disk follows distorted paths, a phenomenon called gravitational lensing that makes the light from behind the black hole bend into a hump over the top and bottom, changing with viewing angle. The event horizon shadow is a dark zone around the horizon about twice as large as the black hole's actual surface.
texte: Due to the gravity of black holes, the accretion disks [music] have a very unique shape. The gravity warps the fabric of the universe, which means that any of the light from the accretion disk must follow that distorted path. This results in a phenomenon known as gravitational [music] lensing. The light that passes over the accretion disk from behind the black hole bends, forming a hump over the top and the bottom of the black hole. The shape changes slightly depending on the angle at which the accretion disk is being viewed. If you're looking at the black hole straight on, the accretion disk has no hump at all. A phenomenon known as the event horizon shadow results [music] from distortion of space-time by gravity around the event horizon. This too causes gravitational lensing of light, which combined with the warping of time-space [music] results in a dark zone around the event horizon, which ends up being around twice as large as the black hole's actual surface. >> [music]
